newsitem.title: USA: Vermont weighs selling $55 mln of debt in Nov, Dec.
newsitem.headline: Vermont weighs selling $55 mln of debt in Nov, Dec.

text.p: Vermont on Thursday said it might sell as much as $55 million of general obligation bonds in two offerings, with the first and larger one expected in November, and a smaller sale planned for December.

Michael Smith, deputy treasurer, who noted the final details of the offerings still are being worked out, said that the first sale would be competitively bid, while the second issue likely will be sold through negotiation.
And the December sale would be a Vermont Citizens Bond, which means that only state residents can buy the bonds.

The two sales, which both will raise new money, will take care of the state's needs for fiscal year 1997, Smith said, adding that before the year ends in June 1997, the state must repay about $105 million of revenue anticipation notes.
